text.content:
Bounty Hunters are masters of the hunt — expert trackers, survivalists, and trappers who form a symbiotic bond with their quarry.

SKILLS

ARMY OF ONE · SL max 3

When you apply the effects of a tool with a target of "One creature", you may spend up to (SL) additional Inventory Points. For every additional Inventory Point you spend this way, you also apply the tool's effects to another creature you can see.

BOUNTY

You gain a new section on your character sheet called a Bounty. Your Bounty can be anything you're hunting or searching for: an NPC, a location, or even an artifact.

You may spend 1 Fabula Point to invoke your Bounty as a Trait to reroll dice, or to invoke it as a Bond, treating its strength value as equal to (1 + your Bounty Hunter level ÷ 5).

You may change the subject of your Bounty after you level up, after you rest, or by spending an Opportunity.

HUNTER'S TOOLS · SL max 5

When you first acquire this Skill, you acquire two tools, and whenever you acquire this Skill again, you acquire two additional tools.

You may perform the Inventory Action and spend an appropriate amount of Inventory Points to apply the effects of one tool you acquired on a target you can see. If a tool requires you to choose an option, you do so when you create that tool, not when you first acquire it.

If a tool's effect deals damage, it deals 5 extra damage if you are level 20 or higher, or 10 extra damage if you are level 40 or higher. If a tool's effect causes Hit Point and/or Mind Point loss and/or recovery, the amount lost and/or recovered increases by 5 if you are level 20 or higher, or by 10 if you are level 40 or higher.

Lastly, if your Bounty is a creature and you deal damage to them with a tool, that damage ignores Resistances.

Your group can also collaboratively create new tools, and the Game Master may opt to include them among rewards, obtained independently of your investment in Hunter's Tools. Each tool is worth approximately 1000 zenit.

The tools, by name, Inventory Point cost and target:

Adrenaline Shot — 3 IP, Self. Until the end of your next turn, each target's Crisis score becomes the same as their Maximum Hit Points value.

Ailment Alloy — 4 IP, Self. Choose one status effect: dazed, shaken, slow or weak. Until the end of the scene or until you use this tool again, creatures who hit a target under the effects of this tool with a melee attack suffer the chosen status effect.

Anticoagulant Round — 2 IP, One creature. Each target suffers 20 physical damage and becomes waned until the end of the scene. If a waned creature recovers Hit Points, instead they recover no Hit Points and stop being waned.

Leather and Asbestos — 4 IP, Self. Each target recovers 10 Hit Points. Then, choose one damage type among air, bolt, earth, fire, or ice: each target gains Resistance to the chosen damage type until the end of the scene or until you use this tool again.

Ruhmkorff Induction Coil — 2 IP, One creature. Each target suffers 20 bolt damage and also suffers slow.

Naphtha Sprayer — 2 IP, One creature. Each target suffers 20 fire damage and also suffers weak.

Magnesium Flash Powder — 2 IP, One creature. Each target suffers 20 light damage and also suffers dazed.

Ice Missile — 2 IP, One creature. Each target suffers 20 ice damage and cannot perform free attacks until the start of your next turn.

Antitoxin — 4 IP, Self. Each target recovers 10 Hit Points. Then, they gain Resistance to poison damage and immunity to poisoned until the end of the scene or until you use this tool again.

Nerve Tonic — 4 IP, Self. Choose up to two status effects: dazed, shaken, slow, or weak. Each target gains immunity to the chosen status effects until the end of the scene or until you use this tool again.

Grapnel and Line — 3 IP, Self. Each target gains the benefits of the Flying Skill until the end of the scene. If the target of this tool was only yourself, you may perform a free attack with a weapon you have equipped, treating your High Roll as 0 when calculating damage.

Magnetic Field Generator — 2 IP, Self. Each target may perform the Guard action for free at the end of their turn. Then, during the next enemy turn, enemies must include each creature affected by this tool among the targets of their attacks and offensive spells, if possible.

Surgical Kit — 3 IP, Self. Each target recovers 20 Hit Points and 20 Mind Points, and they recover from a single status effect of your choice. This tool is considered a potion.

Mind Disruptor — 2 IP, One creature. Each target suffers 20 dark damage and loses 20 Mind Points.

Movement Suppressor — 3 IP, One creature. Until the start of your next turn, attacks and offensive spells without a target of "Special" that are cast by creatures affected by this tool cannot target more than one creature.

Poison Dart — 3 IP, One creature. Each target suffers 20 poison damage and also suffers poisoned.

Reaction Trap — 2 IP, One creature. Until the end of the scene, each target becomes reactive. If a reactive creature attacks or casts a spell outside of their turn, they suffer 10 bolt damage and lose 10 Mind Points. Reactive creatures may spend an action to stop being reactive.

Investigator's Glass — 2 IP, Self. Each target may perform the Study action for free at the end of their turn, gaining a +3 bonus to the Open Check.

Shield-Breaker — 2 IP, One creature. Each target suffers 20 earth damage and cannot perform the Guard action or perform reaction skills related to protecting allies until the start of your next turn.

Smoke Grenade — 4 IP, Self. Each target becomes invisible to all creatures until the start of your next turn. Additionally, when you use this tool, you may immediately fill two sections of any number of Clocks related to escaping, hiding or obstructing light.

Sonic Blaster — 2 IP, One creature. Each target suffers 20 air damage and also suffers shaken.

Mail Undershirt — 3 IP, Self. Each target recovers 10 Hit Points. Then, they gain Resistance to physical damage until the end of the scene or until you use this tool again.

Sticky Bomb — 3 IP, One creature. Each target becomes tagged until the end of the scene. When a tagged creature suffers fire, bolt or physical damage, they stop being tagged and every enemy present in the scene loses 10 Hit Points.

Tonic — 4 IP, Self. Choose one Attribute: Dexterity, Insight, Might, or Willpower. Until the end of the scene or until you use this tool again, each target treats the chosen Attribute as if it were one die size higher (up to a maximum of d12).

Tracker Device — 4 IP, One creature. Until the end of your next turn, each target's Defense score is treated as being equal to their current Dexterity die size, and their Magic Defense score is treated as being equal to their current Insight die size. Additionally, they cannot benefit from the effects of being invisible for the same duration.

Trusty Pocket Knife — 2 IP, Self. Each target may perform the Objective action for free at the end of their turn. Then, if they filled at least one section of a Clock, they may fill one additional section.

Weakening Agent — 2 IP, One creature. Choose one damage type among air, bolt, dark, earth, fire, ice, light or poison: until the end of your next turn, every source that deals damage of the chosen type deals 5 extra damage to each of this tool's targets.

Zap Barrier — 4 IP, Self. Until the end of the scene, each target deals 10 bolt damage to creatures that hit them with melee attacks.

QUICK DRAW · SL max 3

At the start of a conflict scene, you may perform the Inventory Action to produce an elemental shard, a potion or a tool with a total Inventory Point cost equal to or lower than (SL + 2). You cannot use this Skill and the Rogue's High Speed Skill in the same conflict.

SPOILS OF BATTLE · SL max 3

After a conflict ends, if you did not Surrender, you recover (SL + 1) Inventory Points. If you invoked your Bounty at least once during that conflict, you recover 2 extra Inventory Points.
